data.narrative:
Askari Defense is a private Defense & Security company founded by Robert van Zyl, Marc van Zyl, and Benjamin Airdo, at an undisclosed stage with undisclosed prior fundraising. The comparable universe consists of 23 same-sector peers: 2 publicly traded companies (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private firms, including Anduril Industries, Helsing, Shield AI, Saronic, and Quantum-Systems.

Standard peer-median valuation methodology is not applicable here. The Defense & Security peer set, while reasonably sized at 23 companies, lacks sufficient concentration at comparable stage and valuation tier. Filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier comparables yielded fewer than three datapoints in each category, falling below the minimum threshold of three required for robust median analysis. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material distortion given the heterogeneity across development stages and business models within the sector.

Without sufficient stage-aligned private comparables and absent disclosed financial metrics or transaction data for the target, triangulation-based valuation cannot be reliably anchored. Meaningful analysis would require either: disclosure of Askari's stage and prior valuation, additional same-stage peer transactions in Defense & Security, or financial metrics (revenue, growth, burn) to support alternative methods. The identified peer universe provides directional context but insufficient quantitative footing for a point estimate or narrow range.
